relationships.description: The interface is the shared access point through which a collaboration's jointly performed behaviour reaches consumers, so the grouped components' collective value is realized through this endpoint.
relationships.evidence: A gateway, federated GraphQL schema or shared API route configuration mounts the interface as the single entry point fronting several components that are declared together as one collaboration.

relationships.description: The interface cannot operate without the owning or backing component that actually handles the requests arriving on the channel.
relationships.evidence: The controller, gRPC servicer or listener class is registered in the component's module or injects that component's classes, and fails to start or respond if that component is absent.

relationships.description: Requests received on the interface are handled by delegating to an internal function of the component, so the endpoint needs that function to produce its responses.
relationships.evidence: The route handler or RPC method body calls the internal function's method or module directly, as shown in the import graph and call sites.

relationships.description: The interface requires the application service's operations to be available in order to fulfil the calls it accepts on its protocol.
relationships.evidence: The controller or resolver injects the service class and invokes its operations, with the dependency declared in the DI container or constructor signature.

relationships.description: The interface relies on the data object as the request, response or message payload structure it parses and emits on the channel.
relationships.evidence: Handler signatures, OpenAPI/protobuf bindings or listener deserializers reference the data object's class or schema as input or output type.

relationships.description: The interface makes the protected resource reachable to callers, so the resource's permitted operations are invoked through this endpoint and its access controls must apply there.
relationships.evidence: Routes or RPC methods on the interface map to the resource's operations and carry security annotations, guards or policy configuration naming that resource.

relationships.description: The interface is the protocol-specific channel through which the application service's operations are offered to its consumers.
relationships.evidence: The service's operations are bound to routes, RPC methods or topics on this interface in the router, servicer registration or API specification.

relationships.description: Holders of the business role use the interface as their point of access to the application's functionality when carrying out their responsibilities.
relationships.evidence: The interface's authorization configuration, UI/API documentation or access policy names the role as an intended consumer, e.g. role-restricted routes or a role-specific portal endpoint.

notes: delivers-value to ApplicationCollaboration is odd: a traceability value predicate targeting an active-structure grouping; aggregation/assignment fits better. Interface depends-on ApplicationComponent inverts ArchiMate composition (component composed-of interface). depends-on ApplicationService and serves ApplicationService overlap and the latter inverts ArchiMate (service is exposed through/assigned to interface).
